text:
Connor McDavid had a goal and three assists, and he still lost. That's how good Anaheim's middle 20 minutes were in Edmonton.

The Oilers had the start you'd expect. Cutter Gauthier gave the Ducks a power-play lead at 9:26 of the first, Evan Bouchard answered on an Oilers power play late in the period, and early in the second McDavid did something only he does: a shorthanded goal batted out of the air, a chance our numbers put at 2%, to make it 2-1 Edmonton.

Pavel Mintyukov answered barely a minute later. His first goal, at 3:37, was a wrist shot with a 3% chance of going in. His second, at 6:15, was a much better look (49%), and those two goals were worth 0.38 wins, the most of anyone on the ice. Beckett Sennecke, the third overall pick in 2024, then scored late in the second and again on the power play at 1:42 of the third. It was 5-2, Mintyukov had two goals and an assist, and Matt Tomkins had allowed five goals on 21 shots, 1.5 more than those shots deserved.

The Oilers didn't go quietly. They won the third period on chances, 1.56 expected goals to 0.71, and Kasperi Kapanen (16:24, power play) and Leon Draisaitl (19:15) brought it within one, with McDavid assisting on both. Laurent Brossoit held on. Over the full game, our numbers called it a coin flip: Edmonton deserved to win 51% of replays, Anaheim 49%.

Edmonton took 46 penalty minutes, which handed Anaheim eight power plays; the Ducks scored on two of them, the Oilers on two of their six, and McDavid added the shorthanded one. What decided it was goaltending more than process, and that cuts both ways. Anaheim has won three straight. The Oilers, who beat the Ducks 5-2 on Oct. 7, got a vintage McDavid game and a goaltending number they can't live with.
headline: Mintyukov's big night outlasts a four-point McDavid
